findings.F1: The book's loss comes from its timing, not from the market: it earns -0.0396 % a day, of which only -0.0071 % is the coin's own drift on the position held and -0.0325 % is timing. It is short on 51 % of days and long on 45 %, with a mean position of 0.32 of the book. The forecast's direction earns -0.42 % excess per 5-day case (t -2.26, 3254 cases), which is -2.5 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: The learned weights turn the signals against their own useful direction. The momentum component has the sign of the coin's 28-day return on only 45 % of cases (2432), and the reversal component has the sign of the 1-day move on only 41 % (3117). So the correlation learned over the past 365 days is negative more often than positive.
findings.F3: Past power does not carry forward. Cases are split by the sign of the past 365-day weight, and the next 5-day excess return is read in the direction of the raw signal. For the 28-day return it is +0.29 % when the past weight was positive (t 0.85, 1091 cases) and +0.31 % when it was negative (t 1.14, 1341 cases). For the 1-day move it is +0.54 % (t 1.76, 1289) against +0.32 % (t 1.29, 1825). The raw signal predicts the same way whichever sign was learned, so a negative learned weight simply bets against it.
findings.F4: The raw 28-day return predicts the next 5 days in the trend's direction and is graded at its ends. The sign of the 28-day return earns +0.30 % excess per 5-day case (t 1.41, 2432 cases), about 1.6 times a trade's cost. Its top fifth per coin is followed by +1.16 % excess and its bottom fifth by -0.49 %, a spread of 1.66 % (t 2.21, 486 against 490 cases).
findings.F5: The last day's move is followed by more of the same, not by a reversal. Its sign earns +0.41 % excess over the next 5 days (t 2.13, 3117 cases), and its top fifth is followed by +1.05 %. The grading is uneven, though: the second-lowest fifth is followed by -1.58 % and the lowest by +0.43 %. Of the brief's four signals, only these two raw continuation signals have a move per case larger than a trade's cost.
findings.F6: The loss is spread over every year and every coin, so it does not rest on one period. The forecast's signed excess per case is negative in every year from 2019 to 2025 (-0.08 % to -1.27 %) and positive only in 2018 (+1.26 %, 261 cases). It is negative on all six coins (-0.00 % on LTC to -0.91 % on XRP).

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 28-day return, the higher its return over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean with a coin's 4-week trend, more the stronger it is, instead of letting a past-year correlation flip the bet against it.
ideas.name: four-week trend continues

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's move over the last day, the larger its move in the same direction over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat a large daily move as the start of a short continuation and refuse to fade it.
ideas.name: daily move continues five days
